title: The Savior! What a Noble Flame
description: The Savior! What a Noble Flame in Tonic Solfa to ST. AGNES, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: William Cowper wrote these words. They were printed in Olney Hymns (London, 1779), Book II, hymn 55, “Jesus hasting to suffer”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. AGNES; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: The Sa-vior! what a no-ble flame Was kin-dled in his breast, When hast-ing to Je-ru-sa-lem He marched be-fore the rest!

lines: The Savior! what a noble flame
Good-will to men, and zeal for God,
He longs to be baptized with blood,
He pants to reach the cross.
With all his suff'rings full in view,
Forth to the task his spirit flew,
Lord, we return thee what we can!
And while thy bleeding glories here
We learn our lighter cross to bear,

source: John Newton and William Cowper, Olney Hymns (1779)
licence: Public domain: William Cowper died in 1800.
credits: Words by William Cowper (1731–1800), public domain, as printed in Olney Hymns (1779); set to ST. AGNES by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
